sections.overview: The loggerhead sponge is a large Caribbean and south Florida sponge that forms conspicuous structure on shallow hard-bottom habitat.
sections.identification: In Florida Bay it can exceed a metre in diameter and contributes disproportionately to sponge-community biomass.
sections.habitat: In the Florida Keys it occurs on nearshore hard-bottom on both the bay and ocean sides of the islands.
sections.diet: It is a suspension feeder, drawing food particles from the surrounding water.
sections.behavior: Its internal spaces shelter small animals, including snapping shrimps.
sections.reproduction: As a clionaid sponge, it is described as oviparous: sperm and eggs are released into the water, where fertilization and larval development occur.
sections.ecology: Loggerhead sponges create vertical structure and shelter diverse infauna, including snapping shrimps.
sections.conservation: Sponge die-offs in Florida Bay led to restoration research that includes this species; this is a regional habitat concern, not a global status category.
